approaches.name: Direct lateral (Hardinge)
selection_indications: Common exposure for fracture hemiarthroplasty; final selection depends on surgeon experience, patient factors, and institutional practice.
selection_limitations: Abductor splitting and repair are approach-specific concerns.
Comparative evidence does not establish one universally superior approach.
positioning: Supine or lateral positioning may be used according to technique and surgeon preference.
exposure: Center the incision over the greater trochanter, split the iliotibial band, and develop the anterior abductor flap while limiting proximal gluteus medius splitting.
Expose the anterior capsule and femoral neck; repair the abductor mechanism securely to the greater trochanter during closure.

structures_at_risk.protection: Limit proximal extension and avoid blind proximal dissection.
Preserve a repairable flap and obtain secure reattachment.

questions: Q: What is the defining nerve risk of the direct lateral approach? A: The superior gluteal nerve is endangered by excessive proximal abductor splitting.
Q: Why is abductor repair central to closure? A: Failure can produce abductor weakness and Trendelenburg gait.
approaches.coverage_notes: Approach-specific technique is curated; comparative outcome claims are intentionally qualified because current evidence is uncertain.

approaches.name: Posterolateral / posterior (Moore-Southern)
selection_indications: Common alternative for hemiarthroplasty; selection depends on surgeon experience, patient factors, and institutional practice.
selection_limitations: Posterior soft-tissue repair is important for stability.
Comparative evidence is heterogeneous and does not support presenting this as universally preferred.
positioning: Lateral decubitus positioning is used for the AO-described posterolateral approach.
exposure: Split gluteus maximus, identify and tag the short external rotators near their femoral insertion, and reflect them to protect the sciatic nerve while exposing the capsule.
Perform the capsulotomy while preserving the acetabular labrum for hemiarthroplasty; repair the posterior capsule and short external rotators at closure.

structures_at_risk.protection: Respect its posterior location and avoid injurious retractor placement; routine exposure is unnecessary in uncomplicated arthroplasty.

structures_at_risk.structure: Posterior capsule and short external rotators
structures_at_risk.protection: Tag for controlled retraction and subsequent repair.

pitfalls: Failure to repair the posterior capsule and short external rotators
questions: Q: How do the released short external rotators help protect the sciatic nerve? A: They are tagged and reflected posteriorly, creating a soft-tissue layer between the operative field and the nerve.
Q: Which structures should be repaired during posterior closure? A: The posterior capsule and released short external rotator tendons should be securely repaired when feasible.
approaches.coverage_notes: Technique follows AO Surgery Reference; comparative claims are qualified to match the 2025 Cochrane review.
